report.headline: Usage rate projected to fall from 24.9% in the EuroLeague to 18.8% in the NBA, landing just below league average; the true-shooting projection carries no information because the model loses to a trivial baseline on that metric.

projection.text: The model projects an 18.8% usage rate in the NBA, down from 24.9% in the 2022-23 EuroLeague season, with an 80% interval of 13.1% to 24.4% — a span of roughly two standard deviations of the NBA's usage distribution (mean 20.1%, sd 5.6%), so the model can say the role likely shrinks but not by how much.

risks.text: The projected NBA usage rate (18.8%) sits below both the EuroLeague production (24.9%) and even the NBA league average (20.1%), with an 80% interval spanning 13.1% to 24.4% — wide enough that the model is useful for ranking against peers but not for pinning down an individual outcome.
The true-shooting projection is explicitly less accurate than a trivial league-average guess (4.7% error for both), so no efficiency conclusion should be drawn from the 58.4% figure or its interval.
The estimate rests on only 61 historical EuroLeague-to-NBA transitions, a modest sample for a model already carrying substantial prediction-interval width.

strengths.text: Carried a EuroLeague usage rate of 24.9%, nearly a full standard deviation (+0.92 sd) above the league average, indicating a genuine high-usage role rather than an inflated one from a weak team context.
Posted a EuroLeague true shooting percentage of 65.3%, about one standard deviation (+1.01 sd) above league average, reflecting elite efficiency at that usage level.
Combined solid rebounding (8.433 per 75 possessions) with a 12.4% assist rate, suggesting production beyond scoring alone.
Maintained a low turnover rate of 6.9% for a high-usage, high-assist profile.

uncertainty.text: The true-shooting projection of 58.4% should not be treated as informative: its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the NBA league-mean true shooting percentage (also 4.7% error), so the model provides no edge over that trivial baseline for this metric.
